assertions.text: List values in the table use bracket syntax like [tech:java, biz:sales, dev:ci] — not comma-separated strings without brackets.
assertions.evidence: ["tech:java", "dev:python", "biz:sales", "ops:deploy"] uses quoted strings inside brackets, but unquoted colons like tech:java without quotes would parse as maps. The response uses quotes correctly, but the assertion tests whether the notation itself (not just correctness) is demonstrated.

assertions.text: Empty list input uses [] (not a blank cell, which represents null). The distinction between empty list and null is preserved.
assertions.evidence: Row 'Empty tag list returns empty list' shows Tags as [] and Kept? as [], and row 'Null category returns all tags unfiltered' shows Category as blank (null). Both forms appear and are distinct.

assertions.text: Values containing pipes (|), brackets, or colons (:) are properly quoted (e.g. "tech:java") so they don't conflict with table syntax.
assertions.evidence: All tag values with colons are quoted: ["tech:java", "dev:python", ...]. Tags like "tech:java|enterprise" and "tech:report[Q1]" are quoted to preserve special characters.

assertions.text: Set<String> values in the table use curly brace syntax like {tech, dev} — not bracket syntax [tech, dev] which is for lists.
assertions.evidence: Optional column uses {biz}, {tech, ops}, and {} (empty set). These are consistently distinguished from List brackets [].

assertions.text: A cell value containing a newline does not break the table row structure: the newline is either escaped as \n inside the cell, or the value is expressed as a list of lines joined in the test body.
assertions.evidence:

 inside the quoted cell, and the test body calls .replace("\n", "

assertions.text: Values containing pipe characters (|) are quoted so they don't conflict with the markdown table column separator.
assertions.evidence: Row 'Tag with pipe character preserved as-is' shows "tech:java|enterprise" fully quoted, preventing the | from being read as a column separator.

assertions.text: Table has a scenario/description column as the leftmost column
At least one output column name ends with '?' (e.g. 'Filtered tags?' or 'Result?')
Test method body contains no if or switch statements
Annotations appear in order: @DisplayName (if present), @Description (if present), @TableTest — not any other order.
Test method has either a @DisplayName annotation or a method name that reads as a clear, descriptive title when converted from camelCase/snake_case.
assertions.evidence: 3 @TableTest method name(s) read as descriptive titles (no @DisplayName needed)

assertions.text: If @Description is present and the text is longer than a single short line, it uses a text block (triple-quoted string """), not string concatenation with +. Passes if @Description is absent.
assertions.evidence: @Description uses text block or is short single-line

assertions.text: The build file (build.gradle) includes org.tabletest:tabletest-junit as a test dependency
No collection value in any table contains a blank element. `[a, , c]`, `[a, b, ]` and `[, a, b]` are parse errors, not collections holding a null element.
assertions.evidence: All list and set values are well-formed: ["tech:java", "dev:python", ...], {biz}, {tech, ops}, {}. No blank elements appear inside any collection.

assertions.text: An empty tag inside a tag list is written as a quoted empty string ("" or ''), not as a blank element.
assertions.evidence: Row 'Empty tag string is never kept' shows Tag as '' (quoted empty string), not a blank cell. The test filters List.of(resolvedTag) where resolvedTag is the empty string.
